acceptance: Capture the real React/CSS at 320×568, 390×844, 768×1024, 1023×900, 1440×900 and 1920×1080. Approval is conditional on those captures, not this specification.

At 390×844, the live first screen shows the header, fictional context, four counts, all three recent customers and the beginning of the program artwork. Program copy starts below the fold. Count fewer than 40 visible words, including navigation and any valid navigation badges.
Use compact recent progress strings such as 0/5. The Visits or Points section label supplies the unit. Do not achieve the word target by shrinking type, clipping state labels or dropping records.

Check the no-program, draft, live-zero and points first screens separately against the same phone word target. Count point-of-need disclosures separately; no prose block may contain eighteen or more words.
The four default counts reconcile to 10 members, 6 repeat visitors, 1 ready reward instance and 2 redemption events. They are projections, not independent display constants.
The default recent order is June, Ben, Imani. A same-day attempt or Wallet update cannot reorder it.
After Sara’s fifth counted visit, counts are 10, 6, 2, 2 and Sara leads recent customers with Reward ready. After her redemption, counts are 10, 6, 1, 3 and her state is Reward redeemed.
Jasmine’s descent begins at 4 Joined, 3 Came back, 1 Redeemed. Sara’s redemption changes only its final count to 2. This is unique redeemers, unlike the overview’s redemption-event total.
Desktop is a composed spread: four counts across, recent customers beside the program, then a full-width source descent. It must not resemble a centered phone or a grid of statistic cards.
Verify the Loopday artwork’s proposed crop in the actual capture. Record its source and crop in the V3 media manifest. No unrelated café image or invented Jasmine portrait may substitute.
View QR, recording, member detail, attribution, program editing and Wallet composition remain within their specified V3 routes. Opening a destination does not create an event.
Send update means a Wallet update. Its once-per-business-day allowance is checked again by the composer. A disabled allowance never blocks automatic progress updates.
Test a reward-version edit: the program presentation can show a new six-visit rule while existing members correctly retain their five-visit cycles.
Test keyboard-only use, touch, browser Back, restored scroll position, 200% text zoom, reduced motion and safe-area insets. No information may require hover.
No production request, camera permission, Wallet API, pass issuance, notification delivery, database mutation or production session change occurs.
The public sequence is outside this surface. Do not add public-story copy or a promotional sequence to Loyalty Home.
spec.signature_moment: A made-up revenue tile is the forbidden object. In its place, Jasmine’s open 4 → 3 → 1 return descent makes the acquisition source visibly survive the return.

honest_states: Live visits is the initial state. No loading skeleton, fake live indicator, date-range toolbar, comparison percentage or count-up appears.
No program shows no counts, specimen customers, attribution or pretend live card. Create program is the only filled product action.
Draft shows the actual saved rule and last completed step. It has no member counts, usable signup QR, Live label or Send update action.
Live-zero displays four actual zeros. No fake recent rows or nonzero source ledges fill the space.
Points replaces the visits context. It does not add a second active program or translate points into money.
A ready reward and a completed redemption are named states, not green decoration. When more than one reward is ready, a data-derived quantity may accompany Reward ready.
The last Wallet update is a simulated update record, not a sent, delivered or seen notification. An unsaved Wallet never produces a receipt claiming its device changed.
Business-authored updates share one America/Chicago daily allowance. A Google per-pass notification cap is not the same allowance and does not disable card-content updates.
Source counts use unique members. Ready and redeemed overview counts use earned instances and redemption events respectively.
Counter QR is a known acquisition mechanism. Direct signup says Source not tracked. Neither proves an absence of offline creator influence.
Missing media preserves the program rule and actions. An unreadable local provider is an error, not a fabricated zero-member program.
Names, normalized contacts and event records remain fictional and local. Home never exposes contacts or customer identities to a creator context.
spec.two_second_read: Ten members. Six came back. One reward is ready; two were redeemed. Add the next visit.
media: Program artwork: /design-lab/reference-loopday-01.jpg. Build one flat 2:1 brand-artwork band, 358×179 at 390, 296×148 at 320 and 376×188 at 1440. Left 28% is solid #18231D with the coded loop mark; right 72% contains the actual photograph, cover crop at 50% 50%. No lettering is overlaid on the photograph. This crop is proposed for capture review, not claimed already verified.

Program artwork at tablet: 40% of the available content width, 2:1, positioned beside the rule band. At 1920 it follows the four-column width, approximately 411×206. Reserve dimensions before loading; missing media uses #ECEEE5 and Media unavailable at the lower-left with 12px inset.

Coded Loopday mark: a 48×48 square object. A 3px paper stroke follows a circle centered at 24,24 with radius 15, leaving a 40-degree opening centered on the upper-right diagonal. Replace the final 8px of the lower edge of that opening with a straight #B73E28 terminal following its tangent. No enclosing badge, letter, check or stamp. In the artwork band, render at 48px; no-program uses 64px with the same proportions and ink stroke on paper.

Source descent: coded measured rules, not a chart image. Three 3px-high ink segments in 48px lanes share one left datum. Their lengths are proportional to unique-member counts using the largest source Joined count as the common maximum. The final 12px of each positive segment is brick, included within its measured length. Zero has no segment or terminal. Labels remain outside all rules.

No portraits, tiny Wallet screenshot, QR thumbnail, progress-stamp illustration or decorative phone frame appears on Home. Recent customers are text rows. Wallet cards and functional signup QR objects are inspected at their dedicated routes rather than rebuilt as unreadable dashboard decoration.
states: 1. Enter populated visits Home: render the committed local projection immediately, with Business selected and the preserved Home scroll position.
2. Inspect a count: open its definition and one contextual drill-down action. Closing returns focus to the same count without changing data.
3. Inspect Live: show qualified program status. Last Wallet update expands within that panel; View program navigates to the actual program route.
4. Leave for a working task: View QR, Add visit, member, attribution, program or Send update opens its specified V3 route. These destination workflows are not inline Home states.
5. Return after a committed event: read the provider’s new counts, recent order, reward states and source projection. Do not replay scanner, redemption or Wallet-success choreography on Home.
6. Return after a business Wallet update: counts and recent ordering remain unchanged. Last Wallet update reflects the stored simulation; Send update is unavailable until the next business day.
7. Return after a reward edit: show the new active rule in the program presentation. Each member’s row continues to use its own retained cycle version.
8. No program: retain the shell, title and Lab context; replace all operational sections with the loop mark and Turn visits into rewards. Header action becomes Create program.

9. Draft: retain the shell; show actual draft artwork, Free coffee, 5 visits, Draft and Last completed: Reward. Continue setup opens Card. Preview card opens the same creation step focused on its preview without saving or launching.

10. Live-zero: header action becomes View QR; show four zeros and the honest empty recent area. Show the real live program, an empty source explanation and working links. Send update is disabled with its audience reason.
11. Points contexts: replace the visits cohort with the specified single-member points fixture. Header and recent unit change; no five-stroke stamp graphic or arbitrary balance editor appears.

12. Counter QA contexts: Same-day visit, Wallet not added, Google limit reached and Recording error retain valid Home projections until a deliberate downstream action changes them. Selecting a scenario itself does not count a visit.
13. Lab selection: selecting a new scenario or Reset demo opens Change demo state? Only Change state replaces the provider. Cancel retains both local data and current scroll.
14. Asset failure: retain the reserved artwork and all real textual program content. Local state-read failure instead replaces the body with the explicit retry state; do not guess counts.
15. Shared navigation boundary: unimplemented shell destinations open the supplied outside-preview notice. Browser Back dismisses the top layer before leaving Home.

accessibility: Use one h1, semantic section headings and an ordered four-item count group. Each count is a native button with its label and current number in its accessible name.
Count disclosure opening moves focus to its title. Modal phone sheets trap focus, make the background inert and restore focus to the opener on Close, Escape or browser Back.

Recent rows are links, not generic clickable containers. Their accessible names include the first name, full progress unit or reward state, and any ready quantity. Do not expose contact or source text solely in inaccessible hover content.
The compact 0/5 visual is read as 0 of 5 visits; the points equivalent is read with points. These screen-reader expansions are not extra visible captions.
The descent has an accessible textual group naming source and all three counts. Decorative rules, terminals, chevrons and the brand mark are hidden from assistive technology.
All product targets are at least 44×44px. Row and count targets are larger. Disabled Send update has an adjacent explanation connected through its description.
Use the V2 2px brick focus outline with 3px offset on paper. On ink buttons use a clearly contrasting paper inner indicator plus the external outline.
Body copy is 16/24; secondary facts never fall below 13/18, except the established 12px primary-navigation labels. Validate contrast at actual colors, without opacity-muted text.
At 200% text zoom, allow headers, count labels and action bands to grow vertically. Switch the desktop spread to a single content column when its text can no longer fit safely.
Never announce every intermediate projection independently. After a committed return, announce the changed final state once; do not announce decorative chart movement.
Preserve scroll and focus separately for the origin Home and each temporary layer. A route return must not jump to the top merely because a recent row was reordered.
